comments.text:
PREMISE CORRECTED by the fz-kdt.127.1 build (commit f34c2aaa3, base
172ab21f1). The cold review's probe table says sl3dyn under (B) alone
gets "run's callsite, shape test". MEASURED FALSE, both dynamic variants,
head canon byte-identical to base's:

  fixtures2/behavior/same_lambda_two_capture_types_dynamic.fz (mailbox
    scrutinee)  -- `diff` of the backend dumps: no difference at all.
  review/probes/sl3dyn.fz (Process.heap_alloc_stats scrutinee) -- same.

There is no headB/sl3dyn.canon among the review's artifacts (only headA
and headAB), so the row was inferred from A+B rather than measured on B.

WHY it is right that nothing moved, and what it means here. `P.run/2` and
`P.twice/2` are each ONE body over the union
`closure[mk#L](int) | closure[mk#L](float)`, and `twice` calls `f`
INDIRECTLY -- `closure_call ... target=-`. The value's own word selects
the construction wrapper and the wrapper's member selection answers for
the capture layout. No callsite has two targets, so no callsite asks. The
program is correct at base for exactly that reason, and stage (B) has
nothing to add to it.

So this fixture's role in this epic is precisely and only the one the
review's finding F2 gave it: it is the GUARD for THIS ticket. Stage (A)
splits `run` by capture type, main's callsite becomes a 2-target dispatch
in fz-kdt.127's shape, and that is the first moment the dynamic witness
needs the construction axis. This ticket's acceptance should therefore
read: the dynamic fixture stays green AND main's callsite gains a
construction-shape question (`s0 type(closure[P.mk/1#lambda](int))` or
its float twin) -- which is a NEW canon mover for stage (A), not a fact
already true.

Everything else this ticket depends on is in place: an anonymous closure
literal projects to `CallableShapes::any()` (the compose guard), the
capture unpack is keyed on the minting constructions rather than the
function, and the callable axis is PerPosition with containment
admission.
